questions.stem: How often is paediatric spinal anaesthesia used compared with epidural block?
Why is the risk of systemic toxicity low with paediatric spinal anaesthesia?
questions.answer: Small local anaesthetic doses are used

questions.stem: Which group of children may be hard to extubate even after minor surgery?
Which older children with a higher general anaesthesia risk may suit a spinal?
questions.answer: Those with muscular or neuromuscular disease

questions.stem: Under light sedation, which age group cooperates well enough for a spinal?
When is a paediatric spinal contraindicated unless an epidural is also placed?
questions.answer: Surgery expected to last more than 1 hour

questions.stem: Where does the spinal cord usually end in a term neonate?
What is the CSF volume per kg in infants?
What percentage of CSF lies within the spinal canal in infants?
Approximately how deep is the lumbar subarachnoid space at birth?
What is the dose range of heavy bupivacaine for an infant spinal?
Heavy bupivacaine for an infant spinal is 0.07-0.2 mL/kg of a ____ solution.
Why is lidocaine relatively contraindicated for an infant spinal?
questions.answer: Very short block and transient neurological symptoms

questions.stem: What failure rate do infant spinal anaesthetics have?
How common is hypotension with paediatric spinal anaesthesia?
Within how many days do most post-dural puncture headaches resolve conservatively?
What volume of blood is used for a paediatric blood patch after conservative care fails?
How long does a neonatal spinal typically last before regressing?
How predictable is the spread of a neonatal spinal compared with adults?
questions.answer: Less predictable; high blocks are fairly common

questions.stem: What postoperative risk does a neonatal spinal share with general anaesthesia?
What should be planned because a neonatal spinal gives no postoperative analgesia?
questions.answer: Analgesia for when the block wears off suddenly
